# rfc7239 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rfc7239/

## Expand description

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use rfc7239::parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse(header_value) {
    let node = node_result?;
    if let Some(forwarded_for) = node.forwarded_for {
        println!("Forwarded by {}", forwarded_for)
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse an rfc7239 header value into a list of forwarded nodes

# rfc7239

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

## Usage

```
use parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse
```
`no_std`

This crate can be used in a `no_std` environment by disabling the default `std` feature.

The only impact disabling this feature has is using `core::error::Error` and `core::net::IpAddr` instead of the `std` variants and increasing the msrv to 1.81.

# uncased - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uncased/^0.9.10/

## Expand description

Case-preserving, ASCII case-insensitive `no_std` string types.

An *uncased* string is case-preserving. That is, the string itself contains
cased characters, but comparison (including ordering, equality, and hashing)
is ASCII case-insensitive.

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let x: &UncasedStr = "hello!".into();
let y: &UncasedStr = "HelLo!".into();
assert_eq!(x, y);
assert_eq!(x.as_str(), "hello!");
assert_eq!(y.as_str(), "HelLo!");
let x_sub = &x[..4];
let y_sub = &y[..4];
assert_eq!(x_sub, y_sub);
assert_eq!(x_sub.as_str(), "hell");
assert_eq!(y_sub.as_str(), "HelL");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#unicode)Unicode

This crate *does not* perform Unicode case-folding. For Unicode
case-folding, see [ unicase](https://crates.io/crates/unicase).

[§](https://docs.rs#features-and-no_std)Features and `no_std`

Crate features:

- `alloc`(- *default*) - enables the- `Uncased`
- `with-serde`- enables (de)serializing of- `UncasedStr`- `serde`
- `with-serde-alloc`- enables- `alloc`, (de)serializing of- `UncasedStr`- `Uncased`- `serde`

This crate is `#![no_std]` compatible. By default, the `alloc` feature is
enabled, which enables the [ Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html) type but requires

`alloc` support. To
disable the feature, disable this crate’s default features:```
[dependencies]
uncased = { version = "0.9", default-features = false }
```
In addition to the `alloc` feature, support for (de)serializing `UncasedStr`
with `serde` can be enabled via the `with-serde` feature. Support for
(de)serserializing both `UncasedStr` and `Uncased` can be enabled via the
`with-serde-alloc` feature, which implicitly enables the `alloc` feature.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html)- `alloc`
- An uncased (case-insensitive, case-preserving), owned *or*borrowed ASCII string.
- [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)- Str
- A cost-free reference to an uncased (case-insensitive, case-preserving) ASCII string.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AsUncased](https://docs.rs/trait.AsUncased.html)
- Helper trait to convert string-like references to `&UncasedStr`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [eq](https://docs.rs/fn.eq.html)
- Returns true if `s1`and`s2`are equal without considering case.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# polkadot-omni-node 0.18.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/polkadot-omni-node/0.18.0

# Polkadot Omni Node

This is a white labeled implementation based on [ polkadot-omni-node-lib](https://crates.io/crates/polkadot-omni-node-lib).
It can be used to start a parachain node from a provided chain spec file. It is only compatible with runtimes that use block
number

`u32` and `Aura` consensus.## Installation

Download & expose it via `PATH`:

```
# Download and set it on PATH.
```
Replace

`<stable_release_tag>`with the latest stable tag from the[Polkadot SDK releases](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/releases)For example:

Compile & install via `cargo`:

```
# Assuming ~/.cargo/bin is on the PATH
```
## Usage

A basic example for an Omni Node run starts from a runtime which implements the [ sp_genesis_builder::GenesisBuilder](https://docs.rs/sp-genesis-builder/latest/sp_genesis_builder/trait.GenesisBuilder.html).
The interface mandates the runtime to expose a

[.](https://docs.rs/staging-chain-spec-builder/latest/staging_chain_spec_builder/#generate-chain-spec-using-runtime-provided-genesis-config-preset)

`named-preset`### 1. Install chain-spec-builder

**Note**: `chain-spec-builder` binary is published on [ crates.io](https://crates.io) under

[due to a name conflict. Install it with](https://crates.io/crates/staging-chain-spec-builder)

`staging-chain-spec-builder``cargo` like bellow :```
```
### 2. Generate a chain spec

Omni Node requires the chain spec to include a JSON key named `relay_chain`. It is set to a chain id,
representing the chain name, e.g. `westend`, `paseo`, `rococo`, `polkadot`, or `kusama`, but
there are also local variants that can be used for testing, like `rococo-local` or `westend-local`. The
local variants are available only for a build of `polkadot-omni-node` with
`westend-native` and `rococo-native` features respectively.

Additionaly, the `--para-id` flag can be used to set the JSON key named `para_id`. This flag is used
by nodes to determine the parachain id, and it is especially useful when the parachain id can not be
fetched from the runtime, when the state points to a runtime that does not implement the
`cumulus_primitives_core::GetParachainInfo` runtime API. It is recommended for runtimes to implement
the runtime API and be upgraded on chain.

Example command bellow:

### 3. Run Omni Node

And now with the generated chain spec we can start the node in development mode like so:

# git-alias 1.2.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/git-alias/1.2.6

git-alias-1.2.6 is not a library.

                # Git-Alias

一个快速的 Git 别名工具，支持两种调用方式。

## 特性

- **双模式调用**: 支持直接调用 (- `gs`) 和 g 前缀调用 (- `g s`)
- **119+ 内置别名**: 覆盖所有常用 git 操作
- **自定义别名**: 通过- `~/.git-alias.toml`添加自定义别名
- **Shell 补全**: 支持 bash、zsh、fish 补全脚本
- **高性能**: Rust 编译，启动时间 < 1ms

## 安装

```
```

## 配置

### 添加到 PATH

将以下内容添加到 `.bashrc` 或 `.zshrc`:

```
```

## 使用方法

### 基本命令

```
```

### 子命令

## 别名列表

运行 `g list` 查看所有别名。

**调用规则**:

- 直接调用（如 `gs`,`gps`,`gba`）：必须以`g`开头
- `g`前缀调用（如- `g s`,- `g ps`,- `g ba`）：别名不能以- `g`开头
- 以 `g`开头的别名不支持`g`前缀调用（如`g gps`报错）

### Add (添加)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g a` | git add |
| `ga` | git add |
| `g aa` | git add . |
| `gaa` | git add . |

# facett_pipeline - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-pipeline/0.1.10/facett_pipeline/

## Expand description

**facett-pipeline** — a dataflow / Spark **pipeline DAG** viewer + job
progress, brought up to the facett look: **theme-driven** (every colour from
the active [`Theme`]), **animated flowing edges** (a marching-ants sweep along
each edge showing dataflow direction), **per-stage status glow** (running =
pulse, done = steady accent, failed = red bloom via
[`effects::glow_rect`]), and **throughput labels** on edges.

It composes [ facett_graph::DepGraphView](https://docs.rs/facett-graph/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_graph/depgraph/struct.DepGraphView.html) for the

**layout**(toposorted columns) and its

`state_json`, but paints its own animated, themed DAG on top.
A [, and now](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html)

`Facet`**engine-agnostic**: the canonical input is the neutral

[(see](https://docs.rs/model/struct.PipelineModel.html)

`PipelineModel`[), produced by an engine’s](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)

`model`[— so “show another engine’s pipeline” is](https://docs.rs/model/trait.PipelineAdapter.html)

`PipelineAdapter`*a new adapter, not a new viewer*(one-viewer-many-adapters, like facett-graphview). knut ships the Spark/SDP adapter; build with

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.from_model)

`PipelineView::from_model`[. The future graphview render path + extra engine adapters are DEFERRED — see the](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.from_adapter)

`from_adapter`[design note.](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)

`model`[§](https://docs.rs#back-compat)Back-compat

The original surface is unchanged — [ PipelineView::new](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.new),

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.with_progress)

`with_progress`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.counts)

`counts`[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Status.html)

`Status`[all behave as before. The look/animation is](https://docs.rs/struct.JobProgress.html)

`JobProgress`**additive**: themed + animated

**on by default**, switch off with

[; edge throughput labels are opt-in via](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.with_animation)

`with_animation(false)`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html#method.with_throughput)

`with_throughput`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use model::`- [PipelineAdapter](https://docs.rs/model/trait.PipelineAdapter.html);
- `pub use model::`- [PipelineEdge](https://docs.rs/model/struct.PipelineEdge.html);
- `pub use model::`- [PipelineMetrics](https://docs.rs/model/struct.PipelineMetrics.html);
- `pub use model::`- [PipelineModel](https://docs.rs/model/struct.PipelineModel.html);
- `pub use model::`- [Stage](https://docs.rs/model/struct.Stage.html);
- `pub use model::`- [StageMetrics](https://docs.rs/model/struct.StageMetrics.html);
- `pub use model::`- [StageStatus](https://docs.rs/model/enum.StageStatus.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [model](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)
- The **engine-agnostic, normalized pipeline model**— the neutral shape every engine’s adapter produces and the`PipelineView`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Edge](https://docs.rs/struct.EdgeFlow.html)- Flow
- How a single edge animates this frame — the **pure**core of the flowing-edge effect, so the phase math is unit-testable without a painter.
- [JobProgress](https://docs.rs/struct.JobProgress.html)
- Overall job progress (Spark stages/tasks).
- [Pipeline](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineNode.html)- Node
- One pipeline stage/dataset node: its name + status, plus the optional live
detail a real Spark run surfaces — a sublabel (e.g. the output type
`materialized_view`), rows processed, and — for a`Status::Failed`**error message**to surface. Built from a knut`Dataset`+`NodeStatus`by the consumer; the component owns no knut dependency.
- [Pipeline](https://docs.rs/struct.PipelineView.html)- View
- The pipeline view: a DAG + optional job progress, themed + animated.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Status](https://docs.rs/enum.Status.html)
- A dataset/stage run status (generic — map your engine’s status to this).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [edge_](https://docs.rs/fn.edge_phase.html)- phase
- The marching-ants **phase**of an edge at wall-clock`time`(seconds) for a given`speed`(cycles/sec). Pure + deterministic —`phase ∈ [0,1)`, increasing with time, wrapping each cycle.`speed <= 0`freezes the flow at phase 0.
- [human_](https://docs.rs/fn.human_bytes.html)- bytes
- Format a byte count with binary units (`512 B`,`1.0 KiB`,`3.5 MiB`). Mirrors knut’s`human_bytes`so edge/throughput labels read the same.
- [human_](https://docs.rs/fn.human_count.html)- count
- Format a row/record count compactly (e.g. `12.0k`,`3.4M`). Pure + testable; the analogue of`human_bytes`
- [status_](https://docs.rs/fn.status_glow.html)- glow
- The per-stage glow **intensity**in`[0,1]`for`status`at`time`. Running pulses (eased sine), done holds a steady soft glow, failed blooms strongly, idle doesn’t glow. Pure, so the pulse curve is testable.

# facett_osm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-osm/0.1.10/facett_osm/

## Expand description

**facett-osm** — read **OSM GeoParquet** (the `osm2geoparquet` / katana-osm
output) into facett geometry. Each row’s `geometry` column is **WKB** — a
`Point` for nodes, a `LineString`/`Polygon` for ways — which we decode to
`(lon, lat)` points and hand to [ facett_map::MapView](https://docs.rs/facett-map/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_map/struct.MapView.html). This is how facett
gets real OSM data (millions of points) for the map component + its tests.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_wkb.html)- wkb
- Decode a WKB geometry blob, appending every `(lon, lat)`vertex to`out`. Handles Point (1), LineString (2), Polygon (3); ignores Z/M + SRID flags.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_wkb_coords.html)- wkb_ - coords
- Decode a single WKB blob into **one geometry’s**`(lon, lat)`vertices (Point → 1 vertex, LineString → its line, Polygon → its exterior ring), preserving the geometry as a unit (unlike`decode_wkb``read_ways``katana_osm_shared::geometry::decode_coords`.
- [map_](https://docs.rs/fn.map_view.html)- view
- Read a GeoParquet straight into a `facett_map::MapView`
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_points.html)- points
- Read up to `max``(lon, lat)`points from a GeoParquet file’s`geometry`(WKB) column. Works on`osm2geoparquet`’s`nodes.parquet`(Points) and`ways.parquet`(LineStrings → their vertices).
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_points_bytes.html)- points_ - bytes
- Like `read_points`**in-memory**GeoParquet (the bytes of a`nodes.parquet`). This is the filesystem-free path the wasm web demo uses: it`include_bytes!`s a clipped region into the binary and decodes it here (the browser has no`std::fs`). Any`Into<Bytes>`works (`&'static [u8]`,`Vec<u8>`).
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_ways.html)- ways
- Read **ways**(LineString / Polygon geometries) from an`osm2geoparquet``ways.parquet`— the SAME WKB`geometry`column`read_points``tags`column for styling. Each row → a`facett_map::Way``(lon, lat)`, projected to Mercator, classified by its OSM tags through`theme`.`max`caps the number of ways (0 = unlimited). Rows with <2 vertices are skipped (graceful — no panic on a degenerate geometry).
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_ways_bytes.html)- ways_ - bytes
- Like `read_ways`**in-memory**`ways.parquet`(the bytes the wasm web demo`include_bytes!`s — no filesystem in the browser).

---

# autoconf_rs_cli - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/autoconf-rs-cli/0.1.59/autoconf_rs_cli/

## Expand description

autoconf-rs-cli shared library.

Provides the CLI argument parsing harness used by all 8 Autoconf binaries. Each binary is a thin wrapper that delegates to autoconf-rs-core.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Common](https://docs.rs/struct.CommonOpts.html)- Opts
- Common CLI options shared across Autoconf tools.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_input.html)- input
- Read a file into a String, or return stdin contents if path is “-”.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_stdin.html)- stdin
- Read all of stdin into a String.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [CliResult](https://docs.rs/type.CliResult.html)
- Common result type for CLI operations.

Source: https://docs.rs/autoconf-rs-core/0.1.52/autoconf_rs_core/

Emitted by
configure when the project uses LT_INIT/AC_PROG_LIBTOOL. Handles the common automake toolchain:
–mode=compile CC … -c src -o obj.lo   -> .libs/obj.o (PIC) + obj.o + obj.lo descriptor
–mode=link    CC … -o lib.la objs     -> .libs/lib.a (static) + .libs/lib.so (shared) + lib.la
–mode=link    CC … -o prog objs *.la  -> resolves .lo/.la and links the program
–mode=install / –mode=clean            -> best-effort copy / rm macro_overrides  m4 macro definitions injected AFTER aclocal.m4 (so they override the project’s third-party
definitions) and BEFORE configure.ac. autoconf-rs cannot yet correctly expand some standard
third-party macros (notably pkg.m4’s PKG_CHECK_MODULES, whose internals leak
`pkg_default`/`glib_minimum` -> shell syntax errors). We replace them with clean, self-contained
shell that does the real work: run pkg-config at configure time, set PFX_CFLAGS/PFX_LIBS, and
record `@PFX_CFLAGS@`/`@PFX_LIBS@` substitutions into conf_subst.sed (consumed when config files
are created, mirroring confdefs.h -> config.h).

# facett_map3d - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-map3d/0.1.10/facett_map3d/

## Expand description

**facett-map3d** — a **3D map viewer**: the 2D OSM vector basemap
([ facett_map::Way](https://docs.rs/facett-map/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_map/struct.Way.html))

**extruded into 3D**. Building / area footprints become

**prisms**(a closed ring lifted to a height), line ways become flat

**ribbons**laid on the ground, and the whole map sits on a

**terrain plane**. A camera

**orbits**(yaw about Y + a fixed tilt) like

[, so the city reads as a solid, lit, slowly-turning model.](https://docs.rs/struct.RabbitLogo3D.html)

`facett_graph3d::RabbitLogo3D`Two render paths share one [ Facet::ui](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html#tymethod.ui) — the same contract as facett-map and
facett-graph3d:

- **CPU painter**(default, always available, headless-testable) — every extruded triangle is projected (orbit yaw + tilt),- **back-face culled**,- **depth sorted**(painter’s algorithm), and shaded by- `normal·light`. egui tessellates them, so a host with no wgpu RenderState still gets a real lit 3D map. Never panics.
- **wgpu fast path**(feature- `wgpu`) — reuses facett-graph3d’s depth-tested [- `facett_graph3d::logo3d::gpu`] pipeline for the- **znippy rabbit logo overlay**(the spinning mascot in the corner). The basemap prisms always draw on the CPU painter (the headless self-test path), so the GPU is never required.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-synthetic-3d-fixture-is-the-znippy-rabbit-not-squares)The synthetic 3D fixture is the **znippy rabbit** (not squares)

When the host has no real OSM data, [ Map3D::synthetic](https://docs.rs/struct.Map3D.html#method.synthetic) builds the basemap by

**extruding the znippy rabbit silhouette**(

[) — each rabbit loop (body / head / ears) becomes a prism — and pins a 3D](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/rabbit/index.html)

`facett_core::rabbit`[as the logo overlay. So the fixture is a 3D rabbit-shaped skyline, never a placeholder cube.](https://docs.rs/struct.RabbitLogo3D.html)

`facett_graph3d::RabbitLogo3D`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

Pure CPU, inject-assert-testable.**Altitude / LOD lever + the metre calibration**— the single CPU lever that turns the camera’s design-unit dolly distance into a real-world**altitude in metres**, then resolves a`LodTier``< 300 m → reflective water`rule is just one threshold of this lever.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [clip_](https://docs.rs/fn.clip_poly_to_rect.html)- poly_ - to_ - rect
- **Sutherland–Hodgman**clip of a triangle to an axis-aligned- `rect`— the CPU painter’s- **scissor**.- **Moved to**(CONS-CORE Phase A, step 3) and re-exported here so map3d’s public API + its regression fence (- `facett_core::render::cpu::scissor`- `clip_pipeline`/- `frustum_scissor`/- `no_spokes`/- `near_plane_probe`/- `gpu_scissor`) are unchanged. The move is behavior-preserving.- **Sutherland–Hodgman**clip of a triangle (- `tri`) to an axis-aligned- `rect`, returning the clipped convex polygon’s vertices (3..=7 of them) or an empty Vec when the triangle lies wholly outside the rect. This is the CPU painter’s- **scissor**: it geometrically confines every face to the widget rect so nothing a 3D/2D pass paints can land outside the component’s own rectangle — independent of whether the host renderer applies the egui clip_rect as a GPU scissor.
- [clip_](https://docs.rs/fn.clip_tri_frustum.html)- tri_ - frustum
- **Full view-space FRUSTUM clip**(the real fix for the smear) — Sutherland–Hodgman of a triangle against all FIVE relevant frustum planes BEFORE the perspective divide: the near plane- `z >= near`AND the four side planes- `|cx| <= cz·sx`,- `|cy| <= cz·sy`(with- `sx`,- `sy`the projection’s per-axis NDC slopes — for- `project_view`’s focal =- `half_h`,- `sy = 1`,- `sx = half_w/half_h`).
- [clip_](https://docs.rs/fn.clip_tri_near.html)- tri_ - near
- **View-space near-plane clip**(step 1 of the part-step decomposition) — Sutherland–Hodgman clip of a single view-space triangle against the half-space- `z >= near`, returning the clipped convex polygon’s view-space vertices (0 when the whole triangle sits on/behind the eye, 3 when untouched, 4 when one vertex was behind and split). This runs- **before**the perspective divide so no surviving vertex ever divides by a near-zero / negative depth — the geometric replacement for the old “near-singularity spoke reject” + “screen-extent guard” heuristics that let off-axis near faces smear thousands of px off the rect.
- [ink_](https://docs.rs/fn.ink_outside_rect.html)- outside_ - rect
- **Sutherland–Hodgman**clip of a triangle to an axis-aligned- `rect`— the CPU painter’s- **scissor**.- **Moved to**(CONS-CORE Phase A, step 3) and re-exported here so map3d’s public API + its regression fence (- `facett_core::render::cpu::scissor`- `clip_pipeline`/- `frustum_scissor`/- `no_spokes`/- `near_plane_probe`/- `gpu_scissor`) are unchanged. The move is behavior-preserving. The scissor- **oracle**(- `scissor.ink_outside_rect`): count the vertices of the- *scissored*polygons that still land outside- `rect`(beyond- `eps`). A correct scissor leaves- **0**— this is the bug oracle the spec’s clip stage emits (- `ink_outside_rect == 0`). Pure, so both the emit path and tests call it.
- [scissor_](https://docs.rs/fn.scissor_report.html)- report
- **Scissor oracle**(step 7) — measure how far the faces overshoot the widget rect- *before*the rect-scissor confines them, and confirm the clipped output never lands outside. Returns- `(raw_overshoot_px, clipped_escapes)`:

# blueprint_tangle_aggregation_svc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/blueprint-tangle-aggregation-svc/0.2.0-alpha.10/blueprint_tangle_aggregation_svc/

## Expand description

Tangle BLS Signature Aggregation Service

A simple HTTP service that collects BLS signatures from operators, aggregates them once threshold is met, and provides the aggregated result for submission to the Tangle contract.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
Operator 1 ──┐
Operator 2 ──┼──▶ Aggregation Service ──▶ Aggregated Result
Operator 3 ──┘         │
                       ▼
                 Tangle Contract
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#starting-the-service)Starting the service

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use blueprint_tangle_aggregation_svc::{AggregationService, api, ServiceConfig};
use std::sync::Arc;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let service = Arc::new(AggregationService::new(ServiceConfig::default()));
    let app = api::router(service);
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:8080").await.unwrap();
    axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#api-endpoints)API Endpoints

- `POST /v1/tasks/init`- Initialize an aggregation task
- `POST /v1/tasks/submit`- Submit a signature
- `POST /v1/tasks/status`- Get task status
- `POST /v1/tasks/aggregate`- Get aggregated result

[§](https://docs.rs#operator-flow)Operator Flow

- Someone (often the first operator) initializes the task
- Each operator signs the output and submits their signature
- Once threshold is met, anyone can fetch the aggregated result
- Submit the aggregated result to the Tangle contract

# bamboo_agent - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-agent/2026.7.3/bamboo_agent/

## Expand description

Bamboo - A fully self-contained AI agent backend framework

Bamboo provides a complete backend system for AI agents, including:

- Built-in HTTP/HTTPS server (Actix-web)
- Agent execution loop with tool support
- LLM provider integrations (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot)
- Session management and persistence
- Workflow and slash command systems
- Process management for external tools

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Dual mode**: Binary (standalone server) or library (embedded)
- **Unified directory**: All data in the Bamboo data directory (default- `${HOME}/.bamboo`)
- **Production-ready**: Built-in CORS, rate limiting, security headers

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

# rfc7239 0.1.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rfc7239/0.1.3

# rfc7239

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

## Usage

```
use parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse
```
`no_std`

This crate can be used in a `no_std` environment by disabling the default `std` feature.

The only impact disabling this feature has is using `core::error::Error` and `core::net::IpAddr` instead of the `std` variants and increasing the msrv to 1.81.

# rfc7239 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rfc7239/0.1.3/target-redirect/rfc7239/

## Expand description

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use rfc7239::parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse(header_value) {
    let node = node_result?;
    if let Some(forwarded_for) = node.forwarded_for {
        println!("Forwarded by {}", forwarded_for)
    }
}
```

[104](#104)impl<'a> Forwarded<'a> {
[105](#105)    fn parse(forward: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[106](#106)        let mut result = Forwarded::default();
[107](#107)
[108](#108)        let parts = forward.split(';');
[109](#109)
[110](#110)        for part in parts {
[111](#111)            if let Some(i) = part.find('=') {
[112](#112)                let param = UncasedStr::new(&part[..i]);
[113](#113)                let value = &part[i + 1..];
[114](#114)                if param == "by" {
[115](#115)                    result.forwarded_by = Some(NodeIdentifier::parse(value.trim_matches('"'))?);
[116](#116)                }
[117](#117)                if param == "for" {
[118](#118)                    result.forwarded_for = Some(NodeIdentifier::parse(value.trim_matches('"'))?);
[119](#119)                }
[120](#120)                if param == "host" {
[121](#121)                    result.host = Some(value);
[122](#122)                }
[123](#123)                if param == "proto" {
[124](#124)                    result.protocol = Some(value);
[125](#125)                }
[126](#126)            } else {
[127](#127)                return Err(RfcError::MalformedParameter);
[128](#128)            }
[129](#129)        }
[130](#130)
[131](#131)        Ok(result)
[132](#132)    }
[133](#133)}
[134](#134)
[135](#135)impl Display for Forwarded<'_> {
[136](#136)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[137](#137)        let mut needs_delim = false;
[138](#138)        if let Some(ident) = &self.forwarded_for {
[139](#139)            if ident.display_needs_quote() {
[140](#140)                write!(f, "for=\"{}\"", ident)?;
[141](#141)            } else {
[142](#142)                write!(f, "for={}", ident)?;
[143](#143)            }
[144](#144)            needs_delim = true;
[145](#145)        }
[146](#146)        if let Some(ident) = &self.forwarded_by {
[147](#147)            if needs_delim {
[148](#148)                write!(f, ";")?;
[149](#149)            }
[150](#150)
[151](#151)            if ident.display_needs_quote() {
[152](#152)                write!(f, "by=\"{}\"", ident)?;
[153](#153)            } else {
[154](#154)                write!(f, "by={}", ident)?;
[155](#155)            }
[156](#156)            needs_delim = true;
[157](#157)        }
[158](#158)        if let Some(ident) = &self.host {
[159](#159)            if needs_delim {
[160](#160)                write!(f, ";")?;
[161](#161)            }
[162](#162)
[163](#163)            write!(f, "host={}", ident)?;
[164](#164)            needs_delim = true;
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)        if let Some(ident) = &self.protocol {
[167](#167)            if needs_delim {
[168](#168)                write!(f, ";")?;
[169](#169)            }
[170](#170)
[171](#171)            write!(f, "proto={}", ident)?;
[172](#172)        }
[173](#173)
[174](#174)        Ok(())
[175](#175)    }
[176](#176)}

[231](#231)#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[232](#232)pub struct NodeIdentifier<'a> {
[233](#233)    pub name: NodeName<'a>,
[234](#234)    pub port: Option<u16>,
[235](#235)}
[236](#236)
[237](#237)impl<'a> NodeIdentifier<'a> {
[238](#238)    fn parse(name: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[239](#239)        match (name.rfind(':'), name.rfind(']')) {
[240](#240)            (Some(delim), Some(ip6_end)) if delim > ip6_end => {
[241](#241)                Self::parse_name_port(&name[0..delim], Some(&name[delim + 1..]))
[242](#242)            }
[243](#243)            (Some(delim), None) => Self::parse_name_port(&name[..delim], Some(&name[delim + 1..])),
[244](#244)            _ => Self::parse_name_port(name, None),
[245](#245)        }
[246](#246)    }
[247](#247)
[248](#248)    fn parse_name_port(name: &'a str, port: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[249](#249)        Ok(NodeIdentifier {
[250](#250)            name: NodeName::parse(name)?,
[251](#251)            port: port
[252](#252)                .map(u16::from_str)
[253](#253)                .transpose()
[254](#254)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidPort)?,
[255](#255)        })
[256](#256)    }
[257](#257)
[258](#258)    pub fn ip(&self) -> Option<&IpAddr> {
[259](#259)        self.name.ip()
[260](#260)    }
[261](#261)
[262](#262)    fn display_needs_quote(&self) -> bool {
[264](#264)        self.port.is_some() || matches!(self.name, NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V6(_)))
[265](#265)    }
[266](#266)}
[267](#267)
[268](#268)impl Display for NodeIdentifier<'_> {
[269](#269)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[270](#270)        match self.port {
[271](#271)            Some(port) => write!(f, "{}:{}", self.name, port),
[272](#272)            None => write!(f, "{}", self.name),
[273](#273)        }
[274](#274)    }
[275](#275)}

[353](#353)#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[354](#354)pub enum NodeName<'a> {
[355](#355)    Ip(IpAddr),
[356](#356)    Unknown,
[357](#357)    Obfuscated(&'a str),
[358](#358)}
[359](#359)
[360](#360)impl<'a> NodeName<'a> {
[361](#361)    fn parse(name: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[362](#362)        match name {
[363](#363)            "unknown" => Ok(NodeName::Unknown),
[364](#364)            obfuscated if obfuscated.starts_with("_") => {
[365](#365)                if obfuscated
[366](#366)                    .chars()
[367](#367)                    .all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == '_')
[368](#368)                {
[369](#369)                    Ok(NodeName::Obfuscated(obfuscated))
[370](#370)                } else {
[371](#371)                    Err(RfcError::InvalidIdentifier)
[372](#372)                }
[373](#373)            }
[374](#374)            ip6 if ip6.starts_with('[') && ip6.ends_with(']') => ip6[1..ip6.len() - 1]
[375](#375)                .parse()
[376](#376)                .map(IpAddr::V6)
[377](#377)                .map(NodeName::Ip)
[378](#378)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidIdentifier),
[379](#379)            ip4 => ip4
[380](#380)                .parse()
[381](#381)                .map(IpAddr::V4)
[382](#382)                .map(NodeName::Ip)
[383](#383)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidIdentifier),
[384](#384)        }
[385](#385)    }
[386](#386)
[387](#387)    pub fn ip(&self) -> Option<&IpAddr> {
[388](#388)        if let NodeName::Ip(ip) = self {
[389](#389)            Some(ip)
[390](#390)        } else {
[391](#391)            None
[392](#392)        }
[393](#393)    }
[394](#394)}
[395](#395)
[396](#396)impl Display for NodeName<'_> {
[397](#397)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[398](#398)        match self {
[399](#399)            NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V4(ip)) => write!(f, "{}", ip),
[400](#400)            NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V6(ip)) => write!(f, "[{}]", ip),
[401](#401)            NodeName::Unknown => {
[402](#402)                write!(f, "unknown")
[403](#403)            }
[404](#404)            NodeName::Obfuscated(name) => write!(f, "{}", name),
[405](#405)        }
[406](#406)    }
[407](#407)}
[408](#408)

# rfc7239 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rfc7239/latest/rfc7239/

## Expand description

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use rfc7239::parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse(header_value) {
    let node = node_result?;
    if let Some(forwarded_for) = node.forwarded_for {
        println!("Forwarded by {}", forwarded_for)
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

# uncased 0.9.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/uncased/^0.9.10

Case-preserving, ASCII case-insensitive `no_std` string types.

An *uncased* string is case-preserving. That is, the string itself contains
cased characters, but comparison (including ordering, equality, and hashing) is
ASCII case-insensitive.

```
use UncasedStr;
let x: &UncasedStr = "hello!".into;
let y: &UncasedStr = "HelLo!".into;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
See the [documentation](http://docs.rs/uncased) for detailed usage information.

# Usage

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.9"
```
This crate is `#![no_std]` compatible. By default, the `alloc` feature is
enabled, which enables the `Uncased` type but requires `alloc` support. To
disable the feature, disable this crate's default features:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.9",  = false }
```
**Note:** This crate *does not* perform Unicode case-folding. For Unicode
case-folding, see [ unicase](https://crates.io/crates/unicase).

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/^1.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Deserialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.

---

# version_check - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version_check/^0.9/

## Expand description

This tiny crate checks that the running or installed `rustc` meets some
version requirements. The version is queried by calling the Rust compiler
with `--version`. The path to the compiler is determined first via the
`RUSTC` environment variable. If it is not set, then `rustc` is used. If
that fails, no determination is made, and calls return `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

**Note:** Please see [feature detection](https://docs.rs/index.html#feature-detection) for a note on enabling unstable
features based on detection via this crate.

-
Set a `cfg`flag in`build.rs`if the running compiler was determined to be at least version`1.13.0`:`extern crate version_check as rustc; if rustc::is_min_version("1.13.0").unwrap_or(false) { println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=question_mark_operator"); }`See `is_max_version``is_exact_version`*at most*or*exactly*a certain version.
-
Check that the running compiler was released on or after `2018-12-18`:`extern crate version_check as rustc; match rustc::is_min_date("2018-12-18") { Some(true) => "Yep! It's recent!", Some(false) => "No, it's older.", None => "Couldn't determine the rustc version." };`See `is_max_date``is_exact_date`*prior to*or*exactly on*a certain date.
-
Check that the running compiler supports feature flags: `extern crate version_check as rustc; match rustc::is_feature_flaggable() { Some(true) => "Yes! It's a dev or nightly release!", Some(false) => "No, it's stable or beta.", None => "Couldn't determine the rustc version." };`Please see the note on [feature detection](https://docs.rs/index.html#feature-detection).
-
Check that the running compiler supports a specific feature: `extern crate version_check as rustc; if let Some(true) = rustc::supports_feature("doc_cfg") { println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=has_doc_cfg"); }`Please see the note on [feature detection](https://docs.rs/index.html#feature-detection).
-
Check that the running compiler is on the stable channel: `extern crate version_check as rustc; match rustc::Channel::read() { Some(c) if c.is_stable() => format!("Yes! It's stable."), Some(c) => format!("No, the channel {} is not stable.", c), None => format!("Couldn't determine the rustc version.") };`

To interact with the version, release date, and release channel as structs,
use [ Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Date.html)

`Date`[, respectively. The](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html)

`Channel`[function returns all three values efficiently.](https://docs.rs/fn.triple.html)

`triple()`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-detection)Feature Detection

While this crate can be used to determine if the current compiler supports an unstable feature, no crate can determine whether that feature will work in a way that you expect ad infinitum. If the feature changes in an incompatible way, then your crate, as well as all of its transitive dependents, will fail to build. As a result, great care should be taken when enabling nightly features even when they’re supported by the compiler.

One common mitigation used in practice is to make using unstable features
transitively opt-in via a crate feature or `cfg` so that broken builds only
affect those that explicitly asked for the feature. Another complementary
approach is to probe `rustc` at build-time by asking it to compile a small
but exemplary program that determines whether the feature works as expected,
enabling the feature only if the probe succeeds. Finally, eschewing these
recommendations, you should track the `nightly` channel closely to minimize
the total impact of a nightly breakages.

[§](https://docs.rs#alternatives)Alternatives

This crate is dead simple with no dependencies. If you need something more
and don’t care about panicking if the version cannot be obtained, or if you
don’t mind adding dependencies, see
[rustc_version](https://crates.io/crates/rustc_version).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Channel](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html)
- Release channel: “dev”, “nightly”, “beta”, or “stable”.
- [Date](https://docs.rs/struct.Date.html)
- Release date including year, month, and day.
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- Version number: `major.minor.patch`, ignoring release channel.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_exact_date.html)- exact_ - date
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`was released**exactly**on some date.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_exact_version.html)- exact_ - version
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`is**exactly**some version.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_feature_flaggable.html)- feature_ - flaggable
- Checks whether the running or installed `rustc`supports feature flags.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_max_date.html)- max_ - date
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`was released**on or before**some date.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_max_version.html)- max_ - version
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`is**at most**some maximum version.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_min_date.html)- min_ - date
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`was released**on or after**some date.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_min_version.html)- min_ - version
- Checks that the running or installed `rustc`is**at least**some minimum version.
- [supports_](https://docs.rs/fn.supports_feature.html)- feature
- Checks whether the running or installed `rustc`supports`feature`.
- [triple](https://docs.rs/fn.triple.html)
- Reads the triple of `Version``Channel``Date``rustc`.

# uncased - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/uncased/0.9.10/target-redirect/uncased/

## Expand description

Case-preserving, ASCII case-insensitive `no_std` string types.

An *uncased* string is case-preserving. That is, the string itself contains
cased characters, but comparison (including ordering, equality, and hashing)
is ASCII case-insensitive.

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let x: &UncasedStr = "hello!".into();
let y: &UncasedStr = "HelLo!".into();
assert_eq!(x, y);
assert_eq!(x.as_str(), "hello!");
assert_eq!(y.as_str(), "HelLo!");
let x_sub = &x[..4];
let y_sub = &y[..4];
assert_eq!(x_sub, y_sub);
assert_eq!(x_sub.as_str(), "hell");
assert_eq!(y_sub.as_str(), "HelL");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#unicode)Unicode

This crate *does not* perform Unicode case-folding. For Unicode
case-folding, see [ unicase](https://crates.io/crates/unicase).

[§](https://docs.rs#features-and-no_std)Features and `no_std`

Crate features:

- `alloc`(- *default*) - enables the- `Uncased`
- `with-serde`- enables (de)serializing of- `UncasedStr`- `serde`
- `with-serde-alloc`- enables- `alloc`, (de)serializing of- `UncasedStr`- `Uncased`- `serde`

This crate is `#![no_std]` compatible. By default, the `alloc` feature is
enabled, which enables the [ Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html) type but requires

`alloc` support. To
disable the feature, disable this crate’s default features:```
[dependencies]
uncased = { version = "0.9", default-features = false }
```
In addition to the `alloc` feature, support for (de)serializing `UncasedStr`
with `serde` can be enabled via the `with-serde` feature. Support for
(de)serserializing both `UncasedStr` and `Uncased` can be enabled via the
`with-serde-alloc` feature, which implicitly enables the `alloc` feature.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html)- `alloc`
- An uncased (case-insensitive, case-preserving), owned *or*borrowed ASCII string.
- [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)- Str
- A cost-free reference to an uncased (case-insensitive, case-preserving) ASCII string.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AsUncased](https://docs.rs/trait.AsUncased.html)
- Helper trait to convert string-like references to `&UncasedStr`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [eq](https://docs.rs/fn.eq.html)
- Returns true if `s1`and`s2`are equal without considering case.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#138-143)

#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, string: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if `self` starts with any casing of the string `string`;
otherwise, returns `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-9)Example

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let uncased_str = UncasedStr::new("MoOO");
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("moo"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("MOO"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("MOOO"));
assert!(!uncased_str.starts_with("boo"));
let uncased_str = UncasedStr::new("Bèe");
assert!(!uncased_str.starts_with("Be"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("Bè"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("Bè"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("bèe"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("BèE"));
```

# UncasedStr in uncased - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uncased/^0.9.10/struct.UncasedStr.html

`pub struct UncasedStr(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A cost-free reference to an uncased (case-insensitive, case-preserving) ASCII string.

This is typically created from an `&str` as follows:

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let ascii_ref: &UncasedStr = "Hello, world!".into();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#22-168)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-UncasedStr)### impl [UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#22-168)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-UncasedStr)

### impl [UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#61-65)#### pub const fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(string: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)) -> &[UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)

`const_fn_transmute`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#61-65)

#### pub const fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(string: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)) -> &[UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)

**only.**

`const_fn_transmute`Cost-free conversion from an `&str` reference to an `UncasedStr`.

This is a `const fn` on Rust 1.56+.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let uncased_str = UncasedStr::new("Hello!");
assert_eq!(uncased_str, "hello!");
assert_eq!(uncased_str, "Hello!");
assert_eq!(uncased_str, "HeLLo!");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#138-143)#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, string: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#138-143)

#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, string: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if `self` starts with any casing of the string `string`;
otherwise, returns `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
use uncased::UncasedStr;
let uncased_str = UncasedStr::new("MoOO");
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("moo"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("MOO"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("MOOO"));
assert!(!uncased_str.starts_with("boo"));
let uncased_str = UncasedStr::new("Bèe");
assert!(!uncased_str.starts_with("Be"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("Bè"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("Bè"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("bèe"));
assert!(uncased_str.starts_with("BèE"));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#160-167)#### pub fn [into_uncased](https://docs.rs#method.into_uncased)(self: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)>) -> [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html)<'static>

**crate feature **`alloc` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uncased/borrowed.rs.html#160-167)

#### pub fn [into_uncased](https://docs.rs#method.into_uncased)(self: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html)>) -> [Uncased](https://docs.rs/struct.Uncased.html)<'static>

**crate feature**only.

`alloc`Converts a `Box<UncasedStr>` into an `Uncased` without copying or
allocating.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

```
use uncased::Uncased;
let uncased = Uncased::new("Hello!");
let boxed = uncased.clone().into_boxed_uncased();
assert_eq!(boxed.into_uncased(), uncased);
```

# AsUncased in uncased - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uncased/^0.9.10/trait.AsUncased.html

```
pub trait AsUncased {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[as_uncased](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_uncased)(&self) -> &[UncasedStr](https://docs.rs/struct.UncasedStr.html);
}## Expand description

Helper trait to convert string-like references to `&UncasedStr`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use uncased::AsUncased;
let string = "Hello, world!".as_uncased();
assert_eq!(string, "hello, world!");
assert_eq!(string, "HELLO, world!");
assert_eq!(string, "HELLO, WORLD!");
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# eq in uncased - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uncased/^0.9.10/fn.eq.html

## Expand description

Returns true if `s1` and `s2` are equal without considering case.

That is, this function returns `s1.to_ascii_lowercase() == s2.to_ascii_lowercase()`, but does it in a much faster way. This is also
equivalent to `UncasedStr::new(s1) == UncasedStr::new(s2)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
assert!(uncased::eq("ENV", "env"));
assert!(uncased::eq("bRoWN", "BROWN"));
assert!(uncased::eq("hi", "HI"));
assert!(uncased::eq("dogs are COOL!", "DOGS are cool!"));
```

---

# rfc7239 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rfc7239/latest/target-redirect/rfc7239/index.html

## Expand description

Parser for [rfc7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239) formatted `Forwarded` headers.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use rfc7239::parse;
// get the header value from your favorite http server library
let header_value = "for=192.0.2.60;proto=http;by=203.0.113.43,for=192.168.10.10";
for node_result in parse(header_value) {
    let node = node_result?;
    if let Some(forwarded_for) = node.forwarded_for {
        println!("Forwarded by {}", forwarded_for)
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse an rfc7239 header value into a list of forwarded nodes

[96](#96)#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
[97](#97)pub struct Forwarded<'a> {
[98](#98)    pub forwarded_for: Option<NodeIdentifier<'a>>,
[99](#99)    pub forwarded_by: Option<NodeIdentifier<'a>>,
[100](#100)    pub host: Option<&'a str>,
[101](#101)    pub protocol: Option<&'a str>,
[102](#102)}
[103](#103)
[104](#104)impl<'a> Forwarded<'a> {
[105](#105)    fn parse(forward: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[106](#106)        let mut result = Forwarded::default();
[107](#107)
[108](#108)        let parts = forward.split(';');
[109](#109)
[110](#110)        for part in parts {
[111](#111)            if let Some(i) = part.find('=') {
[112](#112)                let param = UncasedStr::new(&part[..i]);
[113](#113)                let value = &part[i + 1..];
[114](#114)                if param == "by" {
[115](#115)                    result.forwarded_by = Some(NodeIdentifier::parse(value.trim_matches('"'))?);
[116](#116)                }
[117](#117)                if param == "for" {
[118](#118)                    result.forwarded_for = Some(NodeIdentifier::parse(value.trim_matches('"'))?);
[119](#119)                }
[120](#120)                if param == "host" {
[121](#121)                    result.host = Some(value);
[122](#122)                }
[123](#123)                if param == "proto" {
[124](#124)                    result.protocol = Some(value);
[125](#125)                }
[126](#126)            } else {
[127](#127)                return Err(RfcError::MalformedParameter);
[128](#128)            }
[129](#129)        }
[130](#130)
[131](#131)        Ok(result)
[132](#132)    }
[133](#133)}
[134](#134)
[135](#135)impl Display for Forwarded<'_> {
[136](#136)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[137](#137)        let mut needs_delim = false;
[138](#138)        if let Some(ident) = &self.forwarded_for {
[139](#139)            if ident.display_needs_quote() {
[140](#140)                write!(f, "for=\"{}\"", ident)?;
[141](#141)            } else {
[142](#142)                write!(f, "for={}", ident)?;
[143](#143)            }
[144](#144)            needs_delim = true;
[145](#145)        }
[146](#146)        if let Some(ident) = &self.forwarded_by {
[147](#147)            if needs_delim {
[148](#148)                write!(f, ";")?;
[149](#149)            }
[150](#150)
[151](#151)            if ident.display_needs_quote() {
[152](#152)                write!(f, "by=\"{}\"", ident)?;
[153](#153)            } else {
[154](#154)                write!(f, "by={}", ident)?;
[155](#155)            }
[156](#156)            needs_delim = true;
[157](#157)        }
[158](#158)        if let Some(ident) = &self.host {
[159](#159)            if needs_delim {
[160](#160)                write!(f, ";")?;
[161](#161)            }
[162](#162)
[163](#163)            write!(f, "host={}", ident)?;
[164](#164)            needs_delim = true;
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)        if let Some(ident) = &self.protocol {
[167](#167)            if needs_delim {
[168](#168)                write!(f, ";")?;
[169](#169)            }
[170](#170)
[171](#171)            write!(f, "proto={}", ident)?;
[172](#172)        }
[173](#173)
[174](#174)        Ok(())
[175](#175)    }
[176](#176)}

[231](#231)#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[232](#232)pub struct NodeIdentifier<'a> {
[233](#233)    pub name: NodeName<'a>,
[234](#234)    pub port: Option<u16>,
[235](#235)}
[236](#236)
[237](#237)impl<'a> NodeIdentifier<'a> {
[238](#238)    fn parse(name: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[239](#239)        match (name.rfind(':'), name.rfind(']')) {
[240](#240)            (Some(delim), Some(ip6_end)) if delim > ip6_end => {
[241](#241)                Self::parse_name_port(&name[0..delim], Some(&name[delim + 1..]))
[242](#242)            }
[243](#243)            (Some(delim), None) => Self::parse_name_port(&name[..delim], Some(&name[delim + 1..])),
[244](#244)            _ => Self::parse_name_port(name, None),
[245](#245)        }
[246](#246)    }
[247](#247)
[248](#248)    fn parse_name_port(name: &'a str, port: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[249](#249)        Ok(NodeIdentifier {
[250](#250)            name: NodeName::parse(name)?,
[251](#251)            port: port
[252](#252)                .map(u16::from_str)
[253](#253)                .transpose()
[254](#254)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidPort)?,
[255](#255)        })
[256](#256)    }
[257](#257)
[258](#258)    pub fn ip(&self) -> Option<&IpAddr> {
[259](#259)        self.name.ip()
[260](#260)    }
[261](#261)
[262](#262)    fn display_needs_quote(&self) -> bool {
[264](#264)        self.port.is_some() || matches!(self.name, NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V6(_)))
[265](#265)    }
[266](#266)}
[267](#267)
[268](#268)impl Display for NodeIdentifier<'_> {
[269](#269)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[270](#270)        match self.port {
[271](#271)            Some(port) => write!(f, "{}:{}", self.name, port),
[272](#272)            None => write!(f, "{}", self.name),
[273](#273)        }
[274](#274)    }
[275](#275)}
[276](#276)

[345](#345)                name: NodeName::Ip("2001:db8:cafe::17".parse().unwrap()),
[346](#346)                port: Some(8080)
[347](#347)            }
[348](#348)        ),
[349](#349)        "[2001:db8:cafe::17]:8080"
[350](#350)    );
[351](#351)}
[352](#352)
[353](#353)#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[354](#354)pub enum NodeName<'a> {
[355](#355)    Ip(IpAddr),
[356](#356)    Unknown,
[357](#357)    Obfuscated(&'a str),
[358](#358)}
[359](#359)
[360](#360)impl<'a> NodeName<'a> {
[361](#361)    fn parse(name: &'a str) -> Result<Self, RfcError> {
[362](#362)        match name {
[363](#363)            "unknown" => Ok(NodeName::Unknown),
[364](#364)            obfuscated if obfuscated.starts_with("_") => {
[365](#365)                if obfuscated
[366](#366)                    .chars()
[367](#367)                    .all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == '_')
[368](#368)                {
[369](#369)                    Ok(NodeName::Obfuscated(obfuscated))
[370](#370)                } else {
[371](#371)                    Err(RfcError::InvalidIdentifier)
[372](#372)                }
[373](#373)            }
[374](#374)            ip6 if ip6.starts_with('[') && ip6.ends_with(']') => ip6[1..ip6.len() - 1]
[375](#375)                .parse()
[376](#376)                .map(IpAddr::V6)
[377](#377)                .map(NodeName::Ip)
[378](#378)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidIdentifier),
[379](#379)            ip4 => ip4
[380](#380)                .parse()
[381](#381)                .map(IpAddr::V4)
[382](#382)                .map(NodeName::Ip)
[383](#383)                .map_err(|_| RfcError::InvalidIdentifier),
[384](#384)        }
[385](#385)    }
[386](#386)
[387](#387)    pub fn ip(&self) -> Option<&IpAddr> {
[388](#388)        if let NodeName::Ip(ip) = self {
[389](#389)            Some(ip)
[390](#390)        } else {
[391](#391)            None
[392](#392)        }
[393](#393)    }
[394](#394)}
[395](#395)
[396](#396)impl Display for NodeName<'_> {
[397](#397)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[398](#398)        match self {
[399](#399)            NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V4(ip)) => write!(f, "{}", ip),
[400](#400)            NodeName::Ip(IpAddr::V6(ip)) => write!(f, "[{}]", ip),
[401](#401)            NodeName::Unknown => {
[402](#402)                write!(f, "unknown")
[403](#403)            }
[404](#404)            NodeName::Obfuscated(name) => write!(f, "{}", name),
[405](#405)        }
[406](#406)    }
[407](#407)}

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:
